title: Tech Concerns Keeping Bonds in The Game
summary:
Tech Concerns Keeping Bonds in The Game 

             
             
            There was some oil price volatility today that looked like it might line up with some of the intraday volatility in the bond market. This may have actually been relevant between 10:10 and 10:30am as various rumors circulated regarding a draft deal. But the general trading range of Treasuries/MBS has been facilitated by the ongoing focus on potential credit concerns for a few key tech names. Coreweave is front and center with today's corporate bond volatility lining up very well with the AM Treasury volatility. Specifically, the height of Coreweave's yield spike lined up perfectly with the best level in Treasuries. Bonds ultimately ended the day slightly stronger--keeping them comfortably in the lower range seen since last Thursday.

title: Mortgage Rates Move Slightly Lower
summary: Mortgage rates dropped 0.03% today on average leaving the top-tier 30yr fixed rate index at 7.40% vs 7.43% yesterday--the third lowest level in more than 3 weeks.  As has been and continues to be the case, the lower rates seen since last Wednesday are primarily being driven by concerns about deleveraging and potential contagion in the AI sector. One of the most closely-watched bellwethers has been Coreweave where a sharp decline in stock prices and sharp increase in corporate bond yields has broadly mirrored recent moves in interest rates.  Some of today's intraday volatility can also be viewed in the context of oil prices and war-related headlines, but we'd caution against placing too much emphasis on the oil price correlation. It's been highly unreliable for more than a month.

title: AI Ass't, Home Equity, Servicing, Borrower Capture, Audit Tools; MISMO & DPA
summary: “I ordered a book online titled, ‘How to Scam People Online.’ It’s been six months and I still haven’t received it.” Being scammed, and fraud in general, isn’t a laughing matter. Companies like SoFi publish information on how to recover afterward. People over 60, as always, are more susceptible. The FBI has a website on mortgage fraud which is well-regarded. Good loan officers are instrumental in teaching their clients about it. I mention all of this because I continue to hear from LOs about how artificial intelligence has increased fraud more than reduced it. Generating one’s own paystubs online takes about 20 seconds, and has for many years, hence the increase in reputable verification services. Third party providers have increased their range and scope: Firstline Compliance, FraudGuard, FundingShield, ACES Quality Management, and Secure Insight all jump to mind. There are even companies like Private Eyes to check the background of those checking the loan. Remember: you have the money, they want it. (Today’s podcast can be found here. This week’s ‘casts are presented by Experian. Experian Verify’s integration with Workday gives mortgage lenders broader access to reliable, up-to-date income and employment data, streamlining verification, enhancing efficiency, and delivering a smoother borrower experience from application to closing. Today’s has an interview with NFTYDoor’s Tim Rowan on home equity lending and how digital technology and human support can improve borrower and loan-originator experiences.)

title: GetWyz Targets First-Time Buyers Before They Reach An LO
summary: GetWyz, a free homeownership planning platform founded by MoneyGuide creator Bob Curtis, launched today on iOS and the web to help first-time buyers estimate when they could afford a home, explore financing options, and plan for expenses after closing.The platform also offers an optional path to GetWyz Mortgage, its wholly owned brokerage — connecting early financial preparation with a potential mortgage provider before buyers begin shopping for a loan.

title: California Probes Lenders Over Delayed Wildfire Insurance Payouts
summary: California regulators are investigating whether lenders improperly delayed insurance payments to Los Angeles wildfire survivors, bringing scrutiny to a funding problem that can complicate borrowers’ plans to rebuild.The Business and Consumer Services Agency and Department of Financial Protection and Innovation announced the inquiry Oct. 15, following more than 160 complaints about insurance disbursements since January 2025.According to the state announcement, regulators are examining delayed payments, access to timely appeals, and instances in which insurance money allegedly remained with a lender after the loan was fully repaid.

title: Home Advantage Brings $55.5M Team Back To West Capital
summary: Home Advantage Lending founder Hass Beydoun is returning to West Capital Lending with his Detroit-based team, citing access to the larger brokerage’s lead-generation infrastructure as a draw.Beydoun joins as vice president, bringing three loan officers, an in-house processor, and the operation’s downtown Detroit office, West Capital announced Monday. The company said it plans to expand the office as part of its Midwest footprint.

title: California Home Sales Drop 6.5%, Prices Keep Climbing
summary: California’s existing-home market is losing transactions without delivering much price relief to buyers, leaving loan originators competing for fewer purchases while affordability remains constrained.Sales of existing single-family detached homes fell 6.5% from a year earlier in September and 3.4% from August, according to the California Association of Realtors’ latest report, released Oct. 19. The statewide median price, meanwhile, rose 1.7% annually to $899,720, slipping just 0.2% from August.

title: Floify Adds Asset Verification, Targets Duplicate Document Requests
summary: Mortgage point-of-sale software provider Floify has added asset verification to Floify Verify, bringing income, employment, and asset checks into a single service and billing relationship while reducing separate steps for borrowers and loan teams.The addition, announced Oct. 20, allows borrowers to connect checking and savings accounts within Floify’s mortgage application. Lenders can also initiate verification during an active loan, configure business rules to trigger requests, and request updated information later.

title: HomeQB And MaxClass Give Originators A New Approach To Professional Referrals
summary: HomeQB combines mortgage planning education, client analysis tools, and marketing materials in a program intended to help loan originators develop referral relationships with financial advisers and other professionals.The approach centers on preparing originators to contribute to conversations about a client’s broader finances, including how borrowing decisions intersect with investments, taxes, and housing needs.

title: One In Three Americans Blame Lenders For Housing Crisis Ahead Of Midterms
summary: Americans want Congress to make housing more affordable. A sizable share also blames the companies financing their homes for the crisis.Thirty-three percent of respondents hold mortgage lenders and banks responsible for the housing affordability crisis, according to a new survey from Clever Real Estate, a low-commission real estate brokerage. That matches the share blaming homebuilders and developers and sits below corporate and institutional investors at 37%. The Trump administration drew blame from 48%.
